questions.stem: A 54-year-old man was brought to the casualty with fever, headache, focal seizures, and right hemiparesis. MRI brain showed hyperintensity in the left frontotemporal region. PCR of his CSF sample was positive for HSV DNA. What would be the drug of choice for this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario and investigations are suggestive of HSV encephalitis for which the drug of choice is intravenous acyclovir. The treatment is effective only if it is started early.

The clinical hallmark of HSV encephalitis is the acute onset of fever and focal neurologic signs with hemorrhagic necrosis of especially the temporal lobe. The most sensitive investigation is HSV DNA demonstration in CSF by PCR.

questions.stem: A patient diagnosed with shingles was prescribed acyclovir. Which of the following statements is false regarding this drug?

options.label: B
options.text: Nephrotoxicity is a dose limiting side effect of acyclovir

options.label: C
options.text: Valacyclovir has a higher bioavailability than acyclovir

options.label: D
options.text: Acyclovir does not enter the CSF

questions.answerText: Acyclovir does not enter the CSF
questions.solutionHtml:
Acyclovir can enter CSF as it is widely distributed into all body fluid compartments, including vesicular fluid and aqueous humor. It can be used for treating shingles caused by HZV.

Option A: Acyclovir is a guanosine nucleoside congener. The other nucleoside congeners are cidofovir, ganciclovir, and famciclovir.

Option B: Nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity, though rare and reversible, are dose-limiting side effects of acyclovir.

Option C: Acyclovir has a low bioavailability which is overcome by administering valacyclovir, a prodrug with higher bioavailability.

Mechanism of action of anti-viral drugs:

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of resistance to acyclovir in HSV-1?
questions.solutionHtml:
The most common cause of resistance to acyclovir in HSV-1 is deficient or absent viral thymidine kinase activity.

Viral thymidine kinase is needed in the conversion of acyclovir to acyclovir triphosphate which competitively inhibits the viral DNA polymerase activity.  

Mutation of viral DNA polymerase is rare.

questions.stem: In which of the following patients can valacyclovir be used as the drug of choice?

options.label: A
options.text: An elderly woman with avian influenza

options.label: D
options.text: An immunocompromised patient with CMV retinitis

questions.solutionHtml:
Oral valacyclovir 1g three times daily for 5-7 days is considered the drug of choice for chickenpox (VZV) in an immunocompetent patient. Treatment should be started ideally within 24 hours of rash onset.

Oral acyclovir (800 mg five times daily) is an alternative drug, but valacyclovir is preferred due to its higher bioavailability and less frequent dosing. In immunocompromised patients, varicella infection is treated with IV acyclovir.

Option A: Oseltamivir is used for the treatment of avian influenza.

Option B: Ribavirin is used for treating RSV bronchiolitis.

Option D: Ganciclovir, foscarnet, and cidofovir are approved for CMV retinitis.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 1107
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition, Page nos. 1335 and 1362

questions.stem: A patient showed persistence of genital herpes lesions even after 7 days of high-dose oral acyclovir therapy. Which of the following antivirals can you use to manage this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
Intravenous foscarnet is used to treat acyclovir-resistant HSV (genital herpes) and VZV infections.

It inhibits viral nucleic acid synthesis by directly inhibiting HSV DNA polymerase (or HIV reverse transcriptase). It is active against herpes simplex, CMV, VZV, and HIV.

Metabolic abnormalities are very common with foscarnet. Symptomatic hypocalcemia and nephrotoxicity are major dose-limiting toxicities of foscarnet. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 1109 and 1112

questions.stem: Which of the following is a true statement about amantadine?

options.label: A
options.text: The most common side effect is CNS toxicity

options.label: B
options.text: It is effective only against Influenza B

options.label: C
options.text: It is routinely used for the treatment of influenza

options.label: D
options.text: It is largely metabolised by the liver

questions.answerText: The most common side effect is CNS toxicity
questions.solutionHtml:
The most common side effect of amantadine is minor CNS toxicity which includes nervousness, difficulty concentrating, and insomnia. It is effective only against Influenza A.

Most strains of influenza are now resistant to amantadine and hence, it is not routinely used for the treatment or prophylaxis of influenza infections. Amantadine is largely excreted unmetabolized in the urine.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 1113
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition, Page no. 1335

questions.stem: A young woman with a recent travel history presented with fever and respiratory difficulty. She was diagnosed with Influenza A and was started on oseltamivir. What is the mechanism of action of this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Oseltamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor.

Drugs like oseltamivir and zanamivir competitively and reversibly interact with the enzyme sites to inhibit viral neuraminidase activity. This interferes with the release of the progeny from infected host cells, halting the spread of infection.

Early administration hastens the resolution of symptoms if given within 48 h of infection. Oseltamivir is given at a dose of 75 mg, twice a day for 5 days for the treatment of influenza A and B. For prophylaxis, it is given at a dose of 75mg, once per day, and continued for the duration of exposure.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology - 14th Edition, Page no 891
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1114
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition, Page no 1338, 1387

questions.stem: Zanamivir is to be given for a patient with an influenza B infection. How will you administer this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Zanamivir is delivered by oral inhalation of dry powder in a lactose carrier. Its oral bioavailability is very low (<5%).

Zanamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor similar to oseltamivir and is active against both influenza A and B.

The different routes of administration of neuraminidase inhibitors are as follows:

  • Zanamivir: Inhalational
  • Oseltamivir: Oral
  • Peramivir: Intravenous




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 1114, 1116

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man is admitted with acute H1N1 influenza pneumonia. He is having severe nausea and vomiting and is not able to take any oral medications. Which of the following drugs can be administered intravenously to him?
questions.solutionHtml:
Peramivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor available for intravenous administration for acute influenza (H1N1).

It is indicated in acute influenza infections where the patient is not able to take drugs via the oral route or if inhalational (zanamivir) formulation is unavailable.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no 1214
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page no 1338

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man, who has history of contact with a known case of influenza, is having fever, cough, and runny nose since today morning. Rapid antigen test turns out to be positive. The endonuclease inhibitor that can be used for his treatment is ___________.
questions.solutionHtml:
The endonuclease inhibitor which can be used for the treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza in adults is baloxavir marboxil.

It is a novel drug that was approved by the FDA in 2018. It is used to treat acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 12 years of age and older who have been symptomatic for less than 48 hours.

It is a selective inhibitor of influenza cap-dependent endonuclease which blocks proliferation by inhibiting mRNA synthesis.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is approved for prophylaxis against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection?
questions.solutionHtml:
Palivizumab is a monoclonal antibody approved for prophylaxis against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection.

It is a humanized monoclonal antibody against F-glycoprotein present on the surface of RSV. It is used in high-risk infants (prematurity and immunosuppressed conditions) and children (with cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases).

The treatment of RSV infections is done with inhaled ribavirin.

Option A: Omalizumab is a monoclonal antibody against IgE indicated in asthma.

Option C: Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody against RANKL indicated in osteoporosis.

Option D: Ribavirin is used for treatment of RSV infections but is not approved for prophylaxis.

questions.stem: A hepatitis B infected patient awaiting liver transplantation is admitted with ascites and encephalopathy. Which of the following is the drug of choice for him?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario of ascites and encephalopathy in a hepatitis B infected patient is suggestive of decompensated liver disease. Tenofovir is the drug of choice for decompensated cirrhosis due to hepatitis B infection.

Tenofovir is one of the first-line drugs for chronic hepatitis B infections. It is available as two prodrug formulations tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF).

Option A: Interferon-alpha is one of the first-line agents in individuals with ongoing HBV-DNA replication and liver inflammation. But it is contraindicated in decompensated cirrhosis with HBV infection as they can precipitate clinical deterioration and increase the risk of bacterial infections.  

Options B and D: Lamivudine and Telbivudine are not considered first-line agents for HBV infections because of the increased frequency of resistance associated with their use.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page nos. 1122 and 1123
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page no 1342

questions.stem: Sofosbuvir is indicated in the treatment of which of the following patients?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sofosbuvir is indicated in the treatment of hepatitis C infection only. It is a directly acting antiviral, NS5B nucleotide polymerase inhibitor.

The goal of treatment in hepatitis C is a sustained virologic response (SVR). It is defined as the absence of a virus in the blood (undetectable HCV RNA), 12 weeks after completion of treatment. This can be achieved by the use of pan-genotypic directly acting antiviral drugs, irrespective of the disease stage.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 1128

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a direct-acting agent (DAAs) used in the treatment of HCV infections?
questions.solutionHtml:
NS4B inhibitors are not direct-acting agents (DAAs).

Direct-acting agents (DAAs) are drugs that target specific viral proteins which are vital to the replication and lifecycle of HCV.

The currently available DAAs inhibit 3 specific non-structural (NS) proteins:

  • NS3/4A protease inhibitors

  • NS5A inhibitors

  • NS5B polymerase inhibitors  





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1127
Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 888

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with history of hepatitis B infection presents with fatigue, vomiting, and weight loss. Her serological markers are given in the table below. What is the treatment of choice for her condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given scenario and serology are suggestive of chronic hepatitis D infection in a hepatitis B carrier for which the treatment of choice is pegylated interferon-alpha (pegIFN-α).

It is the only drug currently available to treat chronic hepatitis D infection.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 1119

questions.stemHtml: A young woman presents with painless warty lesions on the vulva as shown in the image below. Which of the following is a topical agent that can be prescribed for her condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Warty lesions on the vulva as seen in the given image is suggestive of condyloma acuminata caused by HPV (6, 11). Imiquimod is a topical agent with antiviral and immunomodulatory properties indicated in the treatment of external genital and perianal warts.

Other topical agents that can be used include podophyllotoxin and trichloroacetic acid. 





Sharma and Sharma's Principles of Pharmacology 3rd, Page no. 800
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 1285

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is currently approved for the treatment of small pox?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tecovirimat has been recently approved as a treatment of smallpox.

It was approved under the FDA's animal rule, which allows findings from animal studies to support an FDA approval when it is not feasible or ethical to conduct efficacy trials in humans. Cidofovir has also been approved by the FDA for smallpox under this rule.

Both these drugs are currently stockpiled by CDC’s strategic national stockpile, which has the medical supplies required to protect the public in case of a public health emergency.

Tecovirimat could also be used under an investigational new drug (IND) protocol to treat adverse reactions from vaccinia vaccination.

Option B: Lumacaftor is a drug approved for cystic fibrosis.

Option C: Pegvaliase has been approved for the treatment of phenylketonuria in adults.

Option D: Apalutamide is a nonsteroidal antiandrogen medication which is used in the treatment of prostate cancer. It is specifically indicated for use in conjunction with castration in the treatment of non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.





Online Resource, https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/899319
